candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The Nusselt number (Nu) is a dimensionless number representing the ratio of convective to conductive heat transfer across a fluid layer. It is derived from the given physical quantities related to Rayleigh-Bénard convection, which include length (h), temperature difference (delta_T), thermal conductivity (lambda), gravitational acceleration (g), thermal expansion coefficient (alpha), kinematic viscosity (nu), and thermal diffusivity (kappa). The Nusselt number is dimensionless, so all SI exponents are zero.

variables.physical_definition: Height of the container, a length scale of the fluid layer.
Temperature difference between the top and bottom surfaces of the fluid layer.
Thermal conductivity of the fluid, representing the ability to conduct heat.
Gravitational acceleration acting on the fluid.
Thermal expansion coefficient, measuring fractional decrease in fluid density per unit temperature increase at constant pressure.
Kinematic viscosity of the fluid, representing momentum diffusivity.
Thermal diffusivity of the fluid, representing thermal energy diffusivity.

variables.reason: The problem text defines h as the height of the container (vertical separation between hot and cold plates) in a Rayleigh-Bénard layer. The cited record (pq_container_height) is the canonical entry for container height in Rayleigh-Bénard convection, explicitly using symbol h/H and giving si_dimension L (dimension_vector matching [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). This record thus directly identifies h as a pure length in the same physical configuration as the problem.

The problem variable delta_T is defined as the temperature difference between top and bottom surfaces. The cited record (pq_temperature_difference) is the canonical temperature-difference entry (ΔT) with si_dimension Theta (dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,1,0,0]). That record matches the physical meaning in the problem and thus supports the Theta exponent = +1.

The problem names lambda as the thermal conductivity of the fluid. The cited record (pq_thermal_conductivity) is the canonical thermal-conductivity entry in heat-transfer context, lists symbols lambda/λ and gives si_dimension M L T^-3 Theta^-1 (dimension_vector [1,1,-3,0,-1,0,0]). The record explicitly ties lambda to Fourier conduction and therefore applies directly to the problem variable and all nonzero SI coordinates.

The problem variable g denotes gravitational acceleration. The cited record (pq_gravitational_acceleration) is the canonical entry for g with si_dimension L T^-2 (dimension_vector [0,1,-2,0,0,0,0]). This record directly matches the physical meaning and supports the provided L and T exponents.

The problem describes alpha as the coefficient that measures fractional decrease in fluid density per increase in temperature at constant pressure, i.e. the thermal expansion coefficient. The cited record (pq_thermal_expansion_coefficient) is the canonical thermal-expansion entry with si_dimension Theta^-1 (dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,-1,0,0]) and includes the same symbol alpha and domain convection. This record therefore directly supports Theta exponent = -1 for the problem's alpha.

The problem lists nu as the kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity). The cited record (pq_kinematic_viscosity) is the canonical kinematic-viscosity entry (symbol ν) with si_dimension L^2 T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]) and explicitly defines ν as dynamic viscosity divided by density. This matches the problem variable and supports the provided L and T exponents.

The problem names kappa as the thermal diffusivity of the fluid. The cited record (pq_thermal_diffusivity) is the canonical thermal-diffusivity entry (symbols κ, a) with si_dimension L^2 T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]) and defines κ as thermal conductivity divided by density and specific heat. This is the standard meaning used in Rayleigh-Bénard convection and supports the provided exponents.
